disposition_reason: Paired soil and vegetable samples from three Sri Lankan cropping systems were analysed by ICP-OES; Table 7 prints dry-weight means of Cd, Pb, As, Cu and Zn in the edible parts of each crop at each location. Soil values and bioaccumulation factors are not food findings.

study.design: Field survey of paired soil and vegetables with bioaccumulation factors and soil-property correlations
study.origin: Nuwara Eliya, Badulla and Kalpitiya, Sri Lanka (growing fields)
study.method: Washing (root crops scrubbed and peeled), oven drying at 60 C, microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion, ICP-OES (Thermo iCAP 7400)
study.qa: NIST SRM 1573a tomato leaves recoveries Cd 82%, As 84%, Cu 85%, Zn 90%; duplicates and blanks per batch

unresolved: Same sampling campaign (December 2018 to March 2020, same authors) as the Journal of Dry Zone Agriculture paper silva2025-sri-lanka-vegetables-trace-elements-intake, which reports fresh-weight crop means; Table 7 dry-weight location means are new numeric data not printed there, so both are kept but represent the same samples.
Cr was measured in vegetables per the methods but no vegetable Cr values are reported.
Cabbage (Badulla) Cu dispersion printed '3.8.0' is garbled.
Soil total and Mehlich 3 extractable concentrations (Table 3) and BAF values (Figure 1) are not food findings.
